body.acceptance_criteria: The §12 T7 gate: an injected pod failure is triaged, mitigated by an approved write, resolved and postmortemed; a destructive action without the tenant's configured approvals is refused; restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip are callable. The executed suite maps each clause to a named test in T7-acceptance.md; the live cluster script is deploy-bound and is not claimed as run.
body.assignment: The programme architect (conveyor-e2e) is assigned the T7 record: the incident lifecycle over the existing card and approval primitives, the four gated cluster writes, the postmortem/kata loop and the /operations console. The assignment is recorded retrospectively for the 2026-11-27 rework and is bounded by SPEC_V2 §6.5, §9.2 and §12 T7.
body.constraints: The build must not let an ops write reach the cluster without an approval, a recorded dry run and two distinct human approvers; must not let the mitigation wrapper bypass the gate; must not let an incident that needed no write stay unresolvable; must not widen a tool grant; and must not claim the live cluster proof before the deployed image carries the gate. These constraints are the finding acceptance and are carried into the contract.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect owns the record and the acceptance instrument; the Architecture Board approves the Phase A–D set and the contract; T2 supplies the job/event/audit rows; T4 supplies the registry and the destructive effect; T13 owns tools; the web team owns the /operations screen; the on-call operators take the incident decisions; the SRO is accountable for the tranche outcome.
body.retrospective: This Statement of Architecture Work is authored by the 2026-11-27 rework from the SPEC row, the issue #78 delivery, the acceptance evidence and the two fixes at ca155fada. It records the assignment and the acceptance the delivery was measured against; it does not claim a contemporaneous board approval, and it carries the live-proof limitation into the Phase-G review.
body.scope: In scope are the five incident actions, the four write verbs and their gate, the k8s read family, the incident meta lifecycle and the /operations screen. Out of scope are tools and bindings (T13), the agent tool surface (the ops writes are not agent-reachable) and a second ops service; each exclusion is deliberate.

# Project brief — T7 Operations (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Outcome

T7 delivers the operations lifecycle: an incident card is opened, triaged, mitigated through an approved gated write (or a no-action record), postmortemed and resolved; every destructive ops write is refused before the cluster unless it carries an approval, a recorded dry run and two distinct human approvers; and restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip are callable.

## Boundary

In scope are the five incident actions, the four gated write verbs, the k8s read family, the incident meta lifecycle and the /operations console. Out of scope are tools and bindings (T13), the agent tool surface (the ops writes are not agent-reachable) and a second ops service. The boundary is SPEC_V2 §6.5/§9.2 and §12 T7.

## Reuse sources

T7 reuses the existing card and approval primitives (the incident card, the approval and approval_decision rows, the governed_asset postmortem, the process run for the kata), T2's job/event/audit rows and T4's registry and destructive effect. It ships no second ops service and no duplicate of T13's tools.

## Inception units

The delivery unit is issue #78 (PR #438) for the incident lifecycle and the four write verbs, plus PR #434 for the /operations console. The executed evidence is T7-acceptance.md (31 tests, 2026-11-24); the two P1 findings v1-w1b-4 and v1-w3a-5 are fixed at ca155fada.

## Dependencies

T7 depends on T2 (jobs/events/audit), T4 (registry/scopes), T13 (tools) and P0. All are closed; the live cluster proof is deploy-bound on the deployed image carrying ca155fada.

## Acceptance

The acceptance is `acceptance/programme/T7.toml` with 17 checks, backed by the executed suite in T7-acceptance.md: triage, the approved mitigation and read-back, the postmortem and resolution, the refused unapproved write, the callable four verbs, the policy quorum, the systemic kata and the RLS/read family. The live cluster script is not claimed as run.

## Capabilities

The built capability set is sixfold: incident intake, triage and runbooks, the four gated write verbs, mitigation (approved write or no action), the postmortem/kata loop and the /operations console. The §6.5 gate and the no-action mitigation are the two fixes that make the set conformant.

## Plan

The plan is SPEC_V2 §6.5, §9.2 and §12 T7, delivered through #78 and #434. This rework does not rebuild it: it supplies the lifecycle record, closes the project on the executed suite and the two fixes, and carries the live cluster proof as a deploy-bound open item.

# Evidence — T7 Operations (retrospective, 2026-11-27)

## Claim

T7 is built and its acceptance is proven by `acceptance/programme/T7.toml`: an incident is triaged, mitigated through an approved write, postmortemed and resolved; a destructive ops action without the tenant's approvals is refused; restart, scale, rollback and flag-flip are callable; and a one-decision or no-dry-run ops call is refused.

## Evidence

The evidence is docs/evidence/record/evidence/T7-acceptance.md (31 tests, 2026-11-24, the clause map), PRs #438 and #434, the two fixes at ca155fada (the dual-control/dry-run gate and the no-action mitigation) and their tests in destructive_gate.rs, ops.rs and ops_write.rs. The fresh receipt verifies 17 checks green at the snapshot.

## Verification

Verification is `verify-project.py --project T7` at a fresh snapshot: 17 checks plus the gate and closure review, 0 failures. The executed commands are the operations suite named in T7-acceptance.md; the live cluster script is deploy-bound and is not claimed. The findings ledger verifies with scripts/verify-findings.py (200 findings, 185 resolved).

## Links

The links are the SPEC_V2 §12 T7 row, the acceptance manifest, the seven A–D artefacts and the index, the delivery contract, the Phase-G review and the closure review. The delivery is #78/PR #438 and #434; the fixes are ca155fada.

## Gap

The gap is the live cluster proof: scripts/ops-live-proof.sh did not run because the operator CLI is absent and the deployed image predated the lane. The deployed image must carry ca155fada before a live proof can claim the dual-control and no-action behaviour. The residual v1-u5-copilot-gate-quorum finding remains S10's.

At the 2026-11-27 snapshot the project row is active at version 12 (track v2, ADM phase G, capability plateau, tranche 5) with meta.measured_status built; it carries a scope baseline and a charter but no contract, Phase A–D artefact set, Phase-G review or closure evidence. The delivery evidence is PR #438 (the incident lifecycle, the four write verbs and the postmortem) and PR #434 (the /operations console), plus docs/evidence/record/evidence/T7-acceptance.md: 31 tests pass on 2026-11-24 and the clause map covers every §12 T7 clause. The two P1 findings the fresh snapshot found unresolved are fixed at ca155fada: v1-w1b-4 (dual control and a recorded dry run at the invoke boundary) and v1-w3a-5 (a no-action mitigation that lets a zero-write incident be postmortemed and resolved); their tests are in destructive_gate.rs, ops.rs and ops_write.rs. The seed says closed and the record is active; this rework closes the project through the one gate, which resolves the seed/live drift.
